covers.quote: If your organisation uses the documentary–note system, change the citation and style of reference list accordingly.

rules.quote: Cite musical compositions using the author–date system.
rules.violation_condition: Musical compositions are cited using a system other than author–date, without an organisational requirement to use documentary–note.
when: Use author–date by default.
If the organisation uses documentary–note, citations and reference-list entries follow that system instead.
rules.why: G-2: the organisational alternative changes which citation system applies, rather than creating a second check.

rules.quote: The references must be accurate and complete
rules.violation_condition: A musical-composition reference contains factually incorrect information about the work.
when: A musical composition is referenced.
rules.why: Accuracy is a factual check distinct from missing identifying information or malformed reference syntax.

covers.quote: provide all the information someone needs to identify the work properly
Attribute compositions with correct references to help people find a particular piece of music.

rules.quote: The references must be accurate and complete
rules.specification: The page requires enough information to identify the work, but does not define a universal minimum set of identifying details. This is a semantic completeness check, separate from the reference-entry templates.
rules.violation_condition: A musical-composition reference lacks information needed to identify the particular work.
when: A musical composition is referenced.
Assess whether the supplied details identify the particular work, rather than requiring every kind of information mentioned on the page.
rules.why: G-4: the identification statement explains completeness; accuracy remains a separate factual check.

covers.quote: This includes music and audio, and any underlying copyright in the musical composition (for example, lyrics or score).

rules.quote: You must attribute copyright material you reference.
rules.violation_condition: Referenced copyright music or audio, or copyright material underlying a composition, has no attribution.
when: The referenced material is copyright material.
This includes music, audio, lyrics and scores.
rules.why: This is an explicit attribution requirement, distinct from choosing a citation system or formatting a reference.

rules.quote: Include all the details required by open access licences
rules.violation_condition: An attribution omits a detail required by the applicable open access licence.
when: The material is used under an open access licence.
The required details depend on that licence.
rules.why: The licence supplies mandatory attribution details; the parenthetical reading suggestion is writer advice, not another rule.

covers.quote: The Vice-Regal Proclamation 1984 sets out the capitalisation of the National Anthem and ‘Advance Australia Fair’.

rules.quote: Use title case (maximal capitalisation) and quotation marks for Australia’s National Anthem.
rules.violation_condition: The title of Australia’s National Anthem is written with capitalisation other than title case.
when: The title is ‘Advance Australia Fair’.
This is an exception to sentence case for song titles.
rules.why: The anthem has a distinct capitalisation check; its quotation-mark requirement is absorbed into the song-title quotation rule.

covers.quote: For compositions with no given name, use roman type and no quotation marks.
Use italics for long works and compilations, roman type for songs
For individual pieces in the soundtrack, use single quotation marks and roman type.

rules.quote: Use roman type for unnamed compositions
rules.violation_condition: An unnamed composition’s designation, a song title, or an individual soundtrack piece is set in non-roman type.
when: The composition has no given name.
Roman type also applies to song titles and individual pieces within soundtracks.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the repeated roman-type requirement; quotation marks and capitalisation are independently detectable properties.

rules.quote: For compositions with no given name, use roman type and no quotation marks.
rules.violation_condition: An unnamed composition’s generic designation is enclosed in quotation marks.
when: The composition has no given name.
This does not prohibit quotation marks around a separately supplied given or popular title.
rules.why: The prohibition on quotation marks is distinct from the roman-type requirement in the same sentence.

rules.quote: Always use a capital letter for the key of musical compositions.
rules.violation_condition: The letter naming a musical composition’s key is lowercase.
when: A letter denotes the key of a musical composition.
rules.why: This is a separate key-notation check, not a restatement of title styling.

rules.quote: For compositions numbered as one of a series, do not use a full stop for the contraction for the word numero (or ‘number’).
rules.violation_condition: The contraction for numero or number has a full stop when identifying a composition numbered within a series.
when: A composition is numbered as one of a series.
rules.why: The prose following the example states a new punctuation rule and is not part of the preceding example.

rules.quote: Don’t capitalise the generic type of composition.
rules.violation_condition: A generic composition-type term has an unnecessary capital letter.
when: The term names a generic type of composition rather than forming part of a title.
A capital required by sentence position is not an unnecessary capital.
rules.why: This checks generic terminology, independently of the case of named works.

covers.quote: Use the foreign terms if they are part of the title of the composition.

rules.quote: Use the English word for most types of compositions (Table 1).
rules.specification: Limit automatic findings to Table 1: prefer prelude to praeludium; fugue to fuga; symphony or symphonies to sinfonia or sinfoniae; oratorio to oratorium; song or its appropriate plural to lieder, chanson or canzona; duet to duetto or duo; and study to etude. Do not infer additional replacements from ‘most’.
rules.violation_condition: A generic composition type uses a listed non-English term instead of its preferred English equivalent.
when: The word is a generic composition-type term.
Retain a foreign term when it is part of the composition’s title.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: the title exception belongs with the terminology preference; E-4: the proposed checking scope is made explicit.

covers.quote: Use ‘concertos’, not ‘concerti’. The exception is ‘concerti grossi’,* the name for a particular style of composition.

rules.quote: Use the English plural form for most types of compositions (Table 2).
rules.specification: Limit the check to the Table 2 types: concertos, suites, trios, arias, partitas, toccatas, sonatas and cantatas. Do not infer a universal prohibition on foreign plurals from ‘most’.
rules.violation_condition: A generic composition-type plural uses a non-English form where Table 2 prefers an English plural, including ‘concerti’ used outside ‘concerti grossi’.
when: The word is a generic plural composition-type term.
‘Concerti grossi’ is an exception because it names a particular style of composition.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: ‘concertos’ and the ‘concerti grossi’ exception refine the same plural-form check.

covers.quote: ‘Op.’ is the abbreviated form of the Latin ‘opus’, meaning ‘work’.

rules.quote: Always use a full stop with this abbreviation.
rules.violation_condition: The catalogue abbreviation ‘Op’ is missing its full stop.
when: ‘Op.’ is used as the abbreviation of opus in a musical catalogue designation.
rules.why: The body sentence is actionable once its antecedent is retained as context.

covers.quote: Some of the more prolific composers have a catalogue of their own.
‘BWV’ is the shortened form of the German Bach Werke Verzeichnis.

rules.quote: Never spell out these shortened forms.
rules.violation_condition: A composer’s catalogue designation is written out in full instead of using its established shortened form.
when: The text is using a catalogue designation to identify a composition.
This does not treat an explanation of what an abbreviation means as a composition citation.
rules.why: The instruction concerns catalogue identifiers; the preceding expansion supplies context rather than an example of a violation.

rules.quote: Place the titles of songs or short, discrete pieces in single quotation marks.

when: The title identifies a song or a short, discrete piece.
This includes hymns, given or popular titles, and individual pieces within soundtracks.

rules.quote: Use sentence case.
rules.violation_condition: An English-language musical title uses capitalisation other than sentence case, except for Australia’s National Anthem.

covers.quote: If the title is in a language other than English, refer to it in the original language.

covers.quote: Apply the capitalisation rules of that language.

covers.quote: Cite the song when you use someone’s lyrics
If you mention the name of the song in the text, place only the author and the year in parentheses.
If you mention the author in text, put the date in parentheses straight after the author’s name.

rules.quote: Write the name of the song, the author and the year of publication in parentheses when you cite lyrics in a text.

when: Lyrics are cited in running text using author–date.

If the song title is given in the prose, put only the author and year in parentheses.
If the author is named in the prose, put the date in parentheses immediately after the author’s name.
